standard.title: Write legibly with growing fluency
standard.description: write words legibly and with growing fluency using unjoined upper-case and lower-case letters
standard.prior_knowledge: Students write letters with developing formation using unjoined upper- and lower-case letters (Foundation). They have not yet written with growing fluency — consistent letter forms that do not slow down writing production.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can write words legibly with growing fluency using consistent unjoined upper-case and lower-case letters.

nodes.label: Consistent letter formation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can form upper-case and lower-case letters consistently and legibly across a short piece of writing.
nodes.minimum_width: Write a short passage where all letters are correctly formed and legible.
nodes.typical_width: Sustain consistent and legible letter formation across varied writing tasks — short compositions, lists, labels — maintaining correct pencil grip/grasp.
wider: Limited width — consistent letter formation does not vary meaningfully across contexts. Extensions such as speed writing or letter size variation go further in one dimension rather than broadening the skill.

response_modes.reason: Letter formation is a fluency and automaticity task. Students need repeated practice to consolidate accurate, legible formation so that handwriting does not consume cognitive resources needed for composition. Practice and habit-forming is the productive investment — width is thin.

nodes.hinge_reason: If letter formation is not automatic, cognitive load from handwriting displaces the composition capacity needed for all written production tasks — students who must consciously form letters cannot simultaneously plan, draft or edit what they are writing.
success_criteria: Student's letters are recognisably correct and legible across a short piece of writing.
Student demonstrates a functional pencil grip/grasp.

nodes.label: Growing writing fluency
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students write at a pace that does not impede composition — forming letters without significant pausing or re-forming.
nodes.minimum_width: Complete a short timed writing task (e.g. two or three sentences) without significant slowdown due to letter formation difficulty.
nodes.typical_width: Write across varied tasks with growing fluency — speed does not need to be fast, but letter formation should not be the bottleneck for ideas.
wider: Limited width — writing fluency is a developmental capacity built through practice volume, not breadth of contexts.

response_modes.reason: Fluency is built through volume of practice. This is a consolidation node — what students need is more writing time, not more types of writing contexts. Thin width acknowledged.

nodes.hinge_reason: Writing pace that cannot keep up with ideas causes composition to stall regardless of vocabulary or grammar knowledge — students lose their intended ideas before they can be recorded, undermining all subsequent written composition tasks.
success_criteria: Student completes writing tasks without pausing significantly to re-form individual letters.
Writing pace is sufficient that ideas are not lost while forming letters.
